newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S. African admits arson on Winnie Mandela house.
newsitem.headline: S. African admits arson on Winnie Mandela house.

text.p: An apartheid security police sergeant will seek amnesty next month for two arson attacks on Winnie Madikizela-Mandela's house in a remote town where she was exiled in the 1980s, South Africa's truth commission said on Tuesday.
The Truth and Reconciliation Commission said in a statement that its amnesty panel would hear the request on September 4.

Former sergeant Mohonaetse Motsamai, 43, would also request amnesty for the murder of an unnamed person in the Botshabelo township near the Free State provincial capital of Bloemfontein in the 1980s, the commission said. It gave no other details.

Madikizela-Mandela, who was divorced from President Nelson Mandela in 1995, took on his struggle against apartheid when he was jailed. She was banished to the Free State town of Brandfort in 1977 for her defiance.
Using her training as a social worker, she tried to improve the lot of blacks living in Brandfort, helping to set up a soup kitchen, a clinic, a bakery and a sewing group.

But after the house was firebombed in 1985, she returned to her home in Soweto township near Johannesburg in contravention of the state-ordered restrictions on her. Despite threats of legal action, she refused to return and remained in Soweto.
Madikizela-Mandela is a member of the top decision-making organs of the ruling African National Congress and president of its Women's League.
The commission set up by President Mandela has until March next year to investigate the human rights record of the apartheid war and pardon offenders who willingly confess.
